answer: Sybil resistance can require each claimed identity to complete a fresh sequence of modular squarings, with every step depending on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot substantially shorten one chain’s elapsed time; creating many identities therefore demands proportionally more sequential work or waiting. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the result efficiently. Like a canyon channeling a ripple past an ivory marker, the dependency constrains each chain, not all chains collectively.
